records.source_title: Diet and feeding ecology of Testudo graeca ibera in Dobrogea
records.plant_taxon: Taraxacum / Sonchus / Trifolium / Medicago taxa reported in the study
records.plant_part_state: young plant material; exact part varies by observation
records.supports: Wild T. g. ibera were documented consuming plant taxa including Taraxacum, Sonchus, Trifolium and Medicago.
records.does_not_support: Does not establish captive diet percentages, feeding frequency, unlimited use, or equivalence between every species in those genera.

records.source_title: Field observations of Testudo graeca ibera feeding in Bulgaria
records.plant_taxon: Cichorium, Taraxacum, Medicago, Potentilla and Sedum taxa reported
records.supports: Documents wild Ibera feeding observations involving the listed plant genera.
records.does_not_support: Non-quantitative observations do not establish captive diet ratios, feeding frequency, or species-level equivalence for Korean plants within the same genus.

records.supports: Classifies grape vine leaves as Feed in Moderation and specifically permits young fresh leaves in moderation.
records.does_not_support: Does not establish Mediterranean Testudo-specific dose, feeding frequency, diet percentage, unlimited use, or equivalence of the fruit with the leaves.

records.source_title: The Tortoise Table — Hibiscus (Rose of Sharon)
records.supports: Classifies Hibiscus (Rose of Sharon) as Safe to Feed and discusses both flowers and leaves.
records.does_not_support: Does not establish a staple percentage, unlimited feeding, Mediterranean Testudo-specific dose, or safety of similarly named Hypericum species.

records.supports: Classifies the entry as Safe to Feed and states that mulberry leaves may be used as part of a wider varied diet.
records.does_not_support: Does not establish a Mediterranean Testudo-specific percentage or unlimited use; the entry distinguishes leaves from fruit and also spans more than one plant taxon.
